title: Commands
cards/0/title: A button calls a model method
cards/0/body: In MVVM, a button does not call a handler in code-behind. Its Command property is bound to a command in the ViewModel.
cards/1/body: The generated command is named after the method plus "Command".
cards/2/q: Bind the button to the Delete() method
cards/3/body: A command can say "I can't run right now" through CanExecute. The button grays itself out.
cards/4/q: Why put [NotifyCanExecuteChangedFor(nameof(SaveCommand))] on the Name property?
cards/4/options/0: When Name changes, the button asks CanSave again and enables or disables itself
cards/4/options/2: It will not compile without it
cards/4/explain: Otherwise the button never learns that the condition changed.
cards/5/body: If the method is async Task, the generator creates an AsyncRelayCommand. While it runs, the command has IsRunning = true, and you cannot press it again.
cards/6/q: What will the command for the LoadAsync() method be called?
cards/6/options/0: LoadCommand: the Async suffix is dropped
cards/6/explain: The generator strips Async from the name.
cards/7/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/7/options/0: A button with a command disables itself when CanExecute = false
cards/7/options/1: An async Task method gives you an AsyncRelayCommand
cards/7/options/3: Commands must be called from code-behind
cards/7/explain: In MVVM, code-behind is nearly empty.
cards/8/q: Match each term to its meaning
cards/8/pairs/1/1: Generate a command from a method
cards/8/pairs/3/1: The async command is still running
